Locus can then sign in to %1$s for you, asking you first. The AI never sees the password.
The password you just typed is kept on this phone, encrypted. Edit or delete it in Settings → Saved logins.

Locus sends no key or password, and answers any login prompt with an empty reply. Only for throwaway or sandbox machines: anyone who can reach this machine can log in the same way. The host key is still checked.
Notifications and scheduled task results from your own bot.
1. In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /\u2060newbot and copy the token it gives you.\n2. Open your new bot and press Start (or send it any message).\n3. Paste the token here and tap Find my chat.
Leave blank to keep the saved one
No messages yet. Open %1$s in Telegram, press Start, then tap Find my chat again.
This is a group or channel: everyone in it will see your notifications.

The token is stored encrypted on this phone and the AI never sees it. Locus only calls Telegram to send you something; it reads what you send the bot only once here, to find your chat, and while the remote options below are on.
The bot token and chat are deleted from this phone. Notifications and scheduled task results stop going to Telegram.
Approving and sending tasks from Telegram need a private chat with your bot, so only your account can press a button.
Allow and Deny buttons come to this chat when a task working in the background asks.
On until %1$s. Messages to the bot start tasks in a chat called Telegram, or join the one running.
Messages to the bot start tasks in a chat called Telegram. It switches itself off after the time below.
Let Telegram tasks do more than read
Telegram tasks run like a chat, asking before they change anything.
Off: they can look things up, read and answer, but can\'t change files, run commands or send anything.

Anything the safety reviewer flagged, or that must be confirmed (payments, sending, after reading outside content), still needs a tap in Locus; Telegram only says so. While remote mode is on, a notification shows and Locus keeps a connection to Telegram open, which uses some battery. Send /off to the bot to stop it from anywhere.
Anyone who gets into your Telegram account can ask too, and plain approvals can be answered from the same chat. A bot chat isn\'t proof it\'s you, so off is the safe default.
Messages from Telegram are treated as outside content, never as your own words, and only this chat counts. Locus ignores messages sent before remote mode was on, and more than a few a minute.
Give the agent its own mailbox, not your personal one. It reads that inbox, and sending always asks you first.
The saved settings can\'t be read: %1$s Fill in the form to replace them.
Leave blank to keep the saved password
Most providers need an app password here, not the one you sign in with.
Who the mail is from, as people see it
Stored encrypted on this phone. The AI never sees it.
The address, servers and password are deleted from this phone. The agent can\'t read or send mail until you set it up again.
Locus doesn\'t know %1$s. Enter its server settings below.
Thunderbird\'s list has nothing for %1$s. Your provider\'s help pages list its IMAP and SMTP settings.
Filled in from Thunderbird\'s list. Check them, then test the connection.
Asks Thunderbird\'s public list of provider settings. Only “%1$s” is sent, never your address or password.
Usually the email address. Both servers use it.
Filled in from the address for the providers Locus knows. For others, tap Edit and enter them.
Incoming: no IMAP server, so the agent can only send

A plan the agent adapts, not calls it replays.
No limit: the workflow may use any tool your settings allow.
Anything else that changes something asks you first. “Ask” keeps a step\'s approval even when your settings allow it.

Only reads on its own. Anything else asks first.
Can %1$s on its own. Anything else asks first.
No workflows yet. When a task goes well, open its receipt and tap Save as workflow.
Web search and clean page reading for the agent. Free plan: 1,000 credits a month (a search of up to 10 results costs 2, reading a page costs 1).
Web search built for AI agents
Web search built for AI agents. Free plan: 1,000 searches a month, no card needed.

Neural web search. Free: $10 of credits each month (about 1,400 searches), no card needed.
Read repositories and issues; open issues and comment (asks first). Use a fine-grained personal access token.
Push notifications to your other devices through a topic you subscribe to (ntfy.sh or your own server). Scheduled task results go there too (and to Telegram, if set up).
Messages from your own Telegram bot: notify_me and scheduled task results arrive in your chat with it. Make a bot with @BotFather, send it any message, then tap Find my chat.
Give the agent its own mailbox, not your personal one. It reads that inbox, and sending always asks you first.

Deploy workspace folders and check builds, logs and environment variables. Deploys and variable changes ask first. Pick the narrowest scope (a team\'s All Projects, or one project). A Full Account token acting on a team also needs a space and the team ID (team_…).
Publish static folders from the workspace, check deploys and manage environment variables. Deploys and variable changes ask first. Netlify allows 3 API deploys a minute, 100 a day.

Manage DNS records, check or start Cloudflare Pages deployments, and publish workspace folders as workers.dev sites. Changes ask first. Create a custom API token with Zone → DNS → Edit (and Zone → Zone → Read) for your domains, plus Account → Cloudflare Pages → Edit if you use Pages and Account → Workers Scripts → Edit to publish sites. If the token sees several accounts, add a space and the account ID.

Check projects, read data with read-only SQL, run changes and deploy Edge Functions (these always ask first). Create a scoped token limited to your projects with Projects → Read and Database → Read; add Database → Read-write to make changes, Edge Functions → Read (Read-write to deploy), and optionally API Keys → Read and Branches → Read. Key values are never shown to the AI.

Check services, deploys and logs, start deploys, set environment variables, suspend or resume services. Deploys, suspend and resume always ask; variable changes ask. Create the key under Account Settings → API Keys; it acts with your account\'s access (scoped keys are in early access at Render). Variable values are never shown to the AI.
e.g. https://ntfy.sh/a-long-secret-name. If the topic needs a token, add a space and the tk_ token.
For a Full Account token acting on a team, add a space and the team ID (team_…).
If the token sees several accounts, add a space and the account ID.
Reference server from the MCP project
Built into %1$s, on your own server
uv (apk add uv); the first start downloads its Python packages
uv and git (apk add uv git)
Repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions and code security.
GitHub\'s sign-in only works with apps GitHub has registered, so Locus uses a token. For read-only access, end the URL with /mcp/readonly.
access to the repositories you want; classic tokens need repo and read:org
Projects, issues, merge requests and pipelines on GitLab.com.
Self-managed GitLab: use https://<your host>/api/v4/mcp. Your top-level group must allow MCP access.
the MCP tool resource with Execute permission
Find, create and update issues, projects and comments.
For read-only access, end the URL with /mcp/readonly.
Read for read-only; Write to change issues
Errors, issues, traces and releases from your Sentry projects.
To limit it to one organisation or project, add them to the URL: /mcp/<org>/<project>.
Up-to-date docs and code examples for thousands of libraries.
Works without a key at lower rate limits.
Ask questions about any public GitHub repository\'s code and docs.
Search and read official Microsoft and Azure documentation and code samples.
AWS documentation, API references, What\'s New posts and architecture guidance.
Search models, datasets, Spaces, papers and the Hugging Face docs.
Without a token you get the public tools only. Choose extra tools at huggingface.co/settings/mcp.
Read; Write to create repos or run Jobs
The whole Cloudflare API (Workers, DNS, R2, D1…) through search and execute.
only the permissions you want Locus to use
Create, deploy and manage Netlify sites, forms and environment variables.
Services, deploys, logs, metrics and read-only Postgres queries on Render.
a key can reach every workspace you belong to
Projects, services, deployments, variables and logs on Railway.
Tables, SQL, migrations, edge functions, logs and docs for your projects.
Safer: add ?project_ref=<your project>&read_only=true to the URL to stick to one project and run SQL as a read-only user.
Serverless Postgres: projects, branches, SQL and migrations.
Create and manage Prisma Postgres databases, backups and connection strings.
Query and inspect a MongoDB or Atlas database, read-only.
MongoDB\'s hosted server needs a sign-in Locus can\'t do, so this one runs in Linux. Remove --readOnly to allow writes.
Generate and edit UI designs and screens with Stitch, and get their code.
create one in Stitch → Settings → API Keys
Search, read and write pages and databases in your workspace.
Jira issues and Confluence pages through Atlassian\'s Rovo MCP server.
Your organisation\'s admin may need to allow the Rovo MCP server first.
Workspaces, collections, environments and API specs in Postman.
/minimal has the essential tools; use /mcp for all of them (many more tools in every chat). EU accounts: mcp.eu.postman.com with an API key.
Product analytics, feature flags, experiments and error tracking.
Dashboards, metrics, logs and alerts in your Grafana Cloud stack.
Customers, payments, invoices, subscriptions and the Stripe docs.
Use a test-mode key until you trust it with live money.
an agent key; from December 2026 secret and restricted keys stop working
Search the web, scrape pages, map and crawl sites.
Works without a key for search and scraping at low limits.
Web search, extract, crawl and research built for AI agents.
Neural web search and page fetching.
Works without a key at free-tier rate limits.
Web, news, image, video and local search from Brave\'s own index.
Brave has no hosted server, so this runs in Linux. The built-in Brave Search integration does the same without Linux.
Check and control the devices you exposed to Assist on your own Home Assistant.
Turn on the Model Context Protocol Server integration in Home Assistant first (Settings → Devices & services). Create the token under your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens.
a token of a non-administrator user is enough; it sees only what you exposed to Assist
Full access uses /api/mcp: every tool set you enabled, which can include reading all entities, history and logs and calling any action. It needs an administrator\'s token.
Find, add, update and complete your tasks and projects.
Locus opens Todoist\'s sign-in in your browser. The server asks for read and write access to your tasks.
Files, notes, calendar, contacts, tasks and Deck on your Nextcloud.
The address is your server\'s, with https://. Use an app password from Nextcloud → Settings → Security → Devices & sessions, not your login password: you can revoke it there.
Read, write and search files in your workspace.
Status, diffs, log, commits and branches of the repository in your workspace.
Fetch a web page and turn it into Markdown.
A local knowledge graph of entities and relations that persists between chats.
a sign-in token Locus gets once from your server; the password itself isn\'t kept
Your RSS reader: unread articles, feeds and categories.
Settings → API Keys → Create a new API key
Your RSS reader, through its Google Reader API: unread articles and subscriptions.
Profile → API management (enable the API in Administration → Authentication first)
Read-only: marking articles read needs a second token FreshRSS derives from the same secret, which Locus doesn\'t hand to the AI.
Search your scanned documents and read their text.
Read-only. Consider a Paperless user that can only view the documents Locus should see.
Find photos and albums in your Immich library.
Give the key only the asset.read, album.read and user.read permissions. Photo details go to your AI provider when Locus reads them.
Read your home timeline and notifications; post only when you confirm.
Preferences → Development → New application (scopes read:statuses, read:notifications, read:accounts; write:statuses to post)
Posting always asks you first and can\'t be remembered. Leave out write:statuses for a read-only token.
Your to-do lists: find tasks and projects, add tasks.
Settings → API Tokens (give it the tasks and projects permissions)
